extDesc.message: Set up automatic tab refresh with intervals from 30 seconds: custom intervals, force refresh, multiple tabs with countdown, right-click menus, and a keyboard shortcut.

commandToggleRefresh.message: Toggle auto refresh for the current tab

notifStopped.message: An auto refresh task was cancelled (the tab was closed or the page is restricted)

notifSessionLost.message: The login session for $SITE$ has expired. Backup for this site is paused to avoid overwriting good state; please sign in again

btnStart.message: Start auto refresh for this tab

discardedHint.message: - tab sleeping, refresh skipped (wake the tab to resume)

errTabGone.message: Cannot access this tab; reload the page and try again

msgStopped.message: Auto refresh stopped for this tab

msgClamped.message: Minimum custom interval is 30 seconds; set to 30 seconds

restrictHint.message: Browser internal pages (chrome:// etc.) cannot be auto-refreshed

errRestricted.message: Browser internal pages (chrome:// etc.) cannot be auto-refreshed

cookieBackupHint.message: Backs up this site's cookies locally and restores the login after a browser restart. Cookies are stored unencrypted in plaintext - assess the risk yourself

keepAliveHint.message: Periodically injects simulated mouse/keyboard activity into the monitored page to delay server-side login expiry timed by user interaction

httpHeartbeatHint.message: Sends a background request with cookies to the monitored URL every 4 minutes; holds sessions timed by the last request without reloading the page

keepWatchingHint.message: Default: the task stops on a hit. On: keep monitoring and notify only for newly appeared keywords

skipOnActivityHint.message: Skips this refresh if there was real user input within 60 seconds; keep-alive simulation is not mistaken for a human

keepAwakeHint.message: Holds a power lock and keeps the system awake while tasks run - be careful on laptop battery

captchaGuardHint.message: Pauses a task when the page title looks like a bot-check wall, so it does not keep hammering the wall; titles only, no body scan. If a normal page gets paused, use that task's Resume button or just turn this off

webhookHint.message: POSTs JSON to this URL: Discord / Slack / Telegram render a readable message, while ntfy delivers the raw JSON; empty = off

webhookInvalid.message: Invalid URL: it must start with http:// or https:// — with the current value nothing will be sent

notifKeywordHits.message: The monitored page now contains the keyword "$KW$"

notifTaskPausedError.message: The monitored page keeps returning errors (5xx/404); the task is auto-paused and will resume once the page recovers

notifTaskPausedCaptcha.message: The monitored page hit a bot verification wall; the task is auto-paused - pass the check and press Resume

skipDiscardedHint.message: Skips this refresh when the tab has been discarded (unloaded) by the browser; it resumes once the tab is woken

emptyHint.message: No tasks yet: click "Start auto refresh" on any tab.

wechatHint.message: Sends notifications as WeChat template messages straight to Tencent's official API from the extension: no app to install, no server to run, nothing in between. You need a WeChat test account plus four credentials (click Setup)

wechatIntro.message: The WeChat "interface test account" page (scan the QR code to apply, no registration needed) gives you all four values below. The extension calls Tencent's API directly - notifications never pass through a relay server.

wechatSecretHint.message: Pressing "Reset" on the test account page invalidates the old value immediately; refill it here or pushes will fail

wechatOpenIdPlaceholder.message: starts with o (appears under users after you follow)

wechatTplPlaceholder.message: generated when you add a test template

wechatTplHint.message: If the template is rejected or variable names do not match, WeChat rejects the whole message

wechatTplBody.message: The test template body must be exactly these two lines: {{title.DATA}} and {{content.DATA}} - any other variable name renders a blank card.

wechatTestBody.message: This is a test message: if you can read it, WeChat push is set up.

wechatStateIdle.message: On; waiting for the first push

wechatErrToken.message: Push failed: credential or token invalid - check the App ID and secret, then save again

wechatErrAppId.message: Push failed: WeChat rejected the App ID - check that App ID and secret are not swapped

wechatErrOpenId.message: Push failed: invalid openID - use the openID of the WeChat account that follows the test account

wechatErrTemplate.message: Push failed: template ID does not match the template body - it must contain the two lines {{title.DATA}} and {{content.DATA}}

wechatErrIp.message: Push failed: this account requires an IP whitelist. Test accounts do not; a verified service account needs the caller IP added

wechatErrFollow.message: Push failed: this openID has not followed the test account yet - scan its QR code first

wechatErrQuota.message: Push failed: daily API quota used up; it resets tomorrow

wechatErrNetwork.message: Push failed: the request from this machine to WeChat did not go through - check your network and retry

wechatErrOther.message: Push failed: WeChat returned an error - please check the four credentials

wechatGuideHint.message: New here? Apply for a test account, copy four credentials, create a template, send a test message

guideIntro.message: Have the extension push notifications straight to your WeChat: no app to install, no relay server in between. Four steps, about three minutes.

guideStep1Body.message: Open the official WeChat 'interface test account' page in a desktop browser and scan the QR code with WeChat to sign in. It is an official sandbox account: no qualification review, no cost.

guideStep1Body2.message: Then copy three things from that page: appID, appsecret, and the openid on your own row in the user list.

guideStep2Body.message: Further down the same page, find 'template message interface · test template' and add one. The title is up to you (e.g. 'Refresh alert'); the content must be exactly these two lines, braces included:

guideStep2Why.message: Why exactly: the extension fills values in under the variable names title and content. A different name renders a blank card.

guideStep2Body2.message: After saving, copy the template ID shown in the list.

guideStep3Title.message: 3. Paste into the extension and test

guideStep3Body.message: Open the extension popup → tick 'WeChat push' → click 'Setup…' → paste the four values → click 'Send a test message'. If your phone receives a message from the test account, you are done.

guideFixFollow.message: 43004 / not followed: go back to the test account page and scan its QR code to follow it (a service account named '测试号' appears in WeChat), then send again.

guideFixAppId.message: 40013: appID and appsecret are mistyped or swapped.

guideFixTemplate.message: 40037 / 47003: the template content does not match the variables. Use exactly two lines, {{title.DATA}} and {{content.DATA}}.

guideFixIp.message: 40164: that IP needs to be whitelisted. Test accounts do not need this; when using a real official account, add the IP in its console.

guideFixQuota.message: 45009: daily quota used up; it resets tomorrow (the sandbox quota is small but fine for alerts).

guideFixOther.message: Other codes: the WeChat status line in the popup shows the reason directly; send a test message there to reproduce.

guideSafetySync.message: The four credentials live in Chrome's synced storage and follow your Google account to other desktops signed in with it. appsecret is effectively a key to send messages as this account - keep it private.

guideSafetyRoute.message: Notifications go straight from the extension to Tencent's official API: no third-party push provider, no relay server. The trade-off is that the content (page title, URL) passes through Tencent's servers and consumes this account's push quota.

guideSafetyOff.message: Turning the 'WeChat push' switch off stops everything: the extension sends no further requests to Tencent.

guideRisk.message: The test account is an official sandbox and its API may change; if template messages are retired, the fallback is a self-built WeCom app.
